{{Short description|Australian physicist (1925–2018)}}
'''Guy Kendall White''' {{Post-nominals|country=AUS|AM|FAA}} (1925–2018) was an [[Australians|Australian]] [[physicist]] who specialised in [[Low Temperature Physics|low-temperature physics]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Dr Guy White (1925-2018), physicist |url=https://www.science.org.au/learning/general-audience/history/interviews-australian-scientists/dr-guy-white-1925-2018-physicist |access-date=2023-07-05 |website=Australian Academy of Science |language=en}}</ref>

In the 1940s, White was part of what has been described as "the elite [[cryogenics]] group of [[doctorate]] researchers" at the [[Clarendon Laboratory]] at [[University of Oxford|Oxford University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=In Memoriam |url=https://docs.lib.purdue.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?referer=&httpsredir=1&article=1002&context=thermal |access-date=10 July 2023 |website=Purdue e-Pubs {{!}} Purdue University}}</ref>

White served as the chief [[research]] [[scientist]] of Australia's [[CSIRO|Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation]] (CSIRO) from 1969 to 1990.<ref name=":0" />

In 1959, White published his [[textbook]] ''Experimental Techniques in Low-Temperature Physics''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=UNIVERSITY OF WOLLONGONG CITATION DELIVERED BY PROFESSOR K. R. McKINNON, VICE CHANCELLOR OF THE UNIVERSITY OF WOLLONGONG, ON THE OCCASION OF THE ADMISSION OF GUY KENDALL WHITE TO THE DEGREE OF DOCTOR SCIENCE, HONORIS CAUSA, ON 11 MAY 1994 . |url=https://documents.uow.edu.au/content/groups/public/@web/@alumni/documents/doc/uow230540.pdf |access-date=6 July 2023 |website=University of Wollongong}}</ref> This book has been described in 2023 as "still the go-to text" in this field.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Australian Institute of Physics - Long-term investment pays off for Australian quantum sector |url=https://www.aip.org.au/News/13078973 |access-date=2023-07-06 |website=www.aip.org.au}}</ref> 

White was awarded the [[David Syme Research Prize]] by the [[University of Melbourne]] in 1966. He was elected a Fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Science]] in 1970.<ref>{{Cite web |title=White, Guy Kendall |url=https://www.eoas.info/biogs/P003588b.htm |access-date=2023-07-07 |website=Encyclopedia of Australian Science and Innovation |language=en-gb}}</ref> 

In 2000, White was appointed a Member of the [[Order of Australia]] in the General Division for his contributions to physics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Supporting AIEF - News And Media - Australian Indigenous Education Foundation |url=http://www.aief.com.au/news/news-media/article.php?id=11835 |access-date=2023-07-05 |website=www.aief.com.au}}</ref>
